header.title: pLeiden T 31: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Book of the Dead
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:tla:tb:pleiden-t-31:translit, from the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. notes.167.1: mḥt is uncertain: perhaps 'the Filled (Eye)', and in 167.2 perhaps 'anything that fills (the treasury)'. ḥry-tp, 'chief', is usually the chief lector or magician. 167.3 is broken, and the editor marks the suffix in pḥ=w as sic. The names Sherget, Nenget, Irket and Kurshget are not identified and may be foreign.

nodes.text: [The] [writings] [of] [the] *mḥt* which the king's son and chief magician(?) Khaemwaset found under the head of a spirit of the West of Memphis.
[It] is more divine than any *mḥt* of the treasury;
[it] [makes] [itself] [into] a door of fire between spirits and the dead, so as not to let them reach the one who reaches [it] [...] a million times.
[The] [document], secret of form, which the royal scribe and chief magician(?) Amenhotep son of Hapu, justified, found, and he made for himself a protection of the body.
Spoken by Sherget to Nenget, son of Irket:

O Kurshget [...], O bull, lord of the phallus, Horus who raises the arm, may you save me from every evil thing decreed by the mouth, that comes about by the hands of [people], [gods], spirits and the dead.
